lines: Mind the lectern. What do you need?
I can spare a moment. Make it useful.
Come in. The floor is quieter than the doorway.
What are you looking for?
I was about to take a break. Your timing is acceptable.
If this concerns a missing book, begin with the truth.
You look like you have a question and no patience for the index.
Give me a moment to finish this line.
I am listening. Please keep your hands away from the wet ink.
Tell me whether you need an answer or advice.
Close the door behind you, then speak.
I have the records out already. That may save us time.
Go on. I can shelve and listen at once.
If this is urgent, say so before I start guessing.
You found me. What happened?
There is room by the desk if you do not lean on it.
Ask plainly. It saves both of us trouble.
I hope you brought details. They improve nearly every conversation.
Let me put this page somewhere safe first.
All right. Start wherever the facts become clear.
